transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-01-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Park (Redwood AE), Meera Desai (Redwood SE), Jules Carter (Silverfold Head of ML), Priya Nair (Silverfold Infra), Tomás Rivera (Silverfold PM)

Summary (auto):
Quick scoping call to align on model choices for Silverfold's multilingual customer support assistant. Main concerns: context length for long conversations and documents (32k vs 128k), tool-calling for retrieval + ticketing system, and deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC) due to PII/data residency. Agreed to run a short Dedicated pilot and follow up with infra deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- Open model comparisons (instruction-tuned vs chat-optimized; tradeoffs)
- Context length needs (typical convo lengths, docs to ingest)
- Multilingual quality (Spanish/Portuguese/FR/DE)
- Tool-calling (retrieval, db queries, ticket creation)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, SAML, KMS, on-prem option)
- Pricing and pilot scope

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect)
[00:00] Liam (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam Park, account exec for Redwood Inference. Quick intros?
[00:08] Jules: Jules Carter here, Head of ML at Silverfold. We've got Priya and Tomás with me.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, Priya, infra.
[00:14] Tomás: Tomás, product. Hey.
[00:16] Meera (SE): Meera Desai, solutions engineering. Great to meet you.
[00:21] Liam: Sweet. High level, Jules sent the note — you're evaluating open models for a multilingual assistant, lots of long contexts, and some tool integrations for retrieval and ticketing. Want to confirm that's right?
[00:29] Jules: Yeah that's the short of it. We're moving off an old rules-based pipeline; want a single model or model family that can handle multi-turn support threads, attach long ticket histories, do lookups into a knowledge base, and call a ticketing API. Also important: Spanish and Portuguese support, and we need to keep EU customer data in-region or on-prem for some accounts.
[00:46] Meera: Great. Couple of clarifying q's up front — what's your typical concurrency / QPS and what are your max context lengths today?
[00:52] Jules: We're somewhere around 20 QPS average for support intents, maybe 120 peak during cobrowse events. Context length — we often need 20–30k tokens when you include thread history + attached docs; for escalations we sometimes want up to 80k, but that's not all calls.
[01:10] Tomás: And we do multi-doc summarization and retrieval; so context can balloon when we embed long KB pages inline.
[01:17] Liam: OK so 32k is kind of your baseline, 80k is edge case — makes sense. Our platform supports model variants with 32k and higher contexts — for very long ones you typically choose a retrieval-first approach or a long-context variant.
[01:27] Priya: When you say "platform supports", any difference between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? For compliance we need VPC or on-prem options.
[01:33] Meera: Yes. Hosted is fastest to go live but data passes through our hosted control plane, with tenant isolation and SOC2 controls. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with more predictable latency and isolation; Private is the VPC/on-prem option where you can control network egress and KMS. We'll share the private deployment checklist.
[01:51] Jules: Does Dedicated support 128k contexts? That's what we're worried about for escalations.
[01:55] Meera: Short answer: it depends on the model. Most open models that are optimized for very long sequences have different memory and perf characteristics. For 128k you generally need a model and runtime combo that is built for sparse attention or chunked attention. We can run a pilot with a long-context variant — often we run 32k-heavy workloads on Dedicated to get stable throughput.
[02:15] Tomás: When you say "model", are we talking Mistral, Llama-v3, or something else? And how about RAG?
[02:20] Meera: Yep, common contenders: Llama-family (v2/v3 variations), Mistral variants, specialized long-context models like LongForm or Star* models. For instruction-following we lean to chat-tuned checkpoints. For RAG tool-calling, the pattern is to do retrieval embeddings + a lightweight reranker then tool-call from the top result.
[02:38] Jules: Any red flags on hallucinations when pulling KB content? We saw a lot with the model we tested last quarter.
[02:42] Meera: Hallucination is model + prompt + retrieval quality problem. We recommend evaluation with unit prompts and a small eval set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching to keep cost down while maintaining the quality profile you want — and we hook eval alerts into the console.
[02:56] [02:58] Speaker 1 (maybe auto-label): The other thing is language coverage, we need Spanish and Portuguese to be first-class. How do open models compare?
[03:05] Meera: Some models have stronger European Romance language coverage out-of-box (some Mistral versions and Llama v3 are decent), but often fine-tuning and prompt engineering matter. We recommend doing a small multilingual eval with production prompts. We can share multilingual benchmark sheets.
[03:21] Jules: Okay, can you also talk about tool-calling — we want to call our ticketing API and also execute KB searches. How does Redwood handle tool calling and function calling?
[03:30] Liam: We support structured tool-calling patterns; you can configure safe wrappers for external APIs and Redwood can stream function call placeholders so your systems can act on them. For security you can restrict tool scopes and set RBAC. There's also support for a retrieval service we host or you can bring-your-own vector DB and we host only the model.
[03:46] Priya: Bring-your-own vector DB is important — we need it behind our VPC for some customers. If we go Private, can we use our managed vector DB and KMS?
[03:53] Meera: Yes. In Private you can keep vector DB inside your VPC and integrate your KMS/HSM. Our control plane becomes a management layer you run in your private environment. There's an on-prem package if you need air-gapped installs.
[04:06] Tomás: Sounds good. Pricing question — how does token pricing change with Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private?
[04:11] Liam: Hosted is usage-based per token plus per-request primitives. Dedicated is usually a committed capacity with monthly reserved commit and lower unit token cost, plus a base seat. Private is enterprise licensing + infra fee. I'll send a matrix.
[04:23] Jules: For the pilot we'd prefer a Dedicated reserved pool for a 2-week test to get real latency numbers. Is that doable?
[04:28] Meera: Absolutely. We typically provision a small Dedicated pool, run scripted traffic patterns (your QPS + escalations), and measure latency/throughput and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:37] [04:38] Priya: And what about SLAs and failover? If a Dedicated pool fails, can we fallback to Hosted?
[04:43] Meera: Yes — routing policies allow fallback to Hosted or other region pools. You can set policy priorities. Also, we support canary rollouts and automatic model fallbacks if a model regresses.
[04:54] Jules: On security: SOC2 is a must, and SAML SSO for console access. Also audit logs for every request, ideally token-level cost breakdowns for us.
[05:02] Liam: We have SOC2 and can provide the report. SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported; audit logs and token-level analytics are surfaced in Redwood Console. I'll attach the SOC2 and SAML configuration guide.
[05:12] Tomás: One nit — when you say "token-level cost", how granular? We want to attribute cost by product route and team.
[05:18] Meera: Token-level with route/model breakdowns. You can tag requests with metadata for ownership. That's the console's standard.
[05:24] Jules: For automated evaluation, do you support regression alerts when model quality drops? We saw some drift when we retried a new quantized variant.
[05:31] Meera: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks and can send alerts based on your prompt sets. You can lock models and only allow rollout after passing your eval thresholds.
[05:39] [05:40] Speaker 2 (minor crosstalk): Does Redwood handle quantization for cost savings? We saw big drops in quality from naive 4-bit runs.
[05:46] Meera: We do quantization-friendly execution paths and recommendations. Often the 4-bit route works for many tasks but for sensitive LLM outputs you might pick mixed precision or keep high-precision for certain layers. We'll recommend quantization profiles per model.
[05:58] Jules: OK what's the timeline we are aiming for? We want a pilot in Feb, and potential rollout to a subset of EU customers by April.
[06:05] Liam: That sounds feasible. Action plan: we send docs and pricing by end of week, Meera drafts the benchmark and pilot plan by next Monday, and we schedule infra deep-dive with Priya for Jan 26.
[06:16] Priya: I'm available that day after 14:00 CET.
[06:19] Meera: Noted. We'll invite time.
[06:22] Tomás: A few more clarifying things on dev workflow — how do we do model versioning and rollbacks?
[06:27] Meera: You can pin model versions per route. Rollouts support canary and A/B testing. We keep KV cache consistency and handle KV cache warmups during rollout.
[06:36] Jules: One more — multilingual evaluation: can you run our Spanish prompts on both Llama-v3 variants and Mistral in the pilot?
[06:43] Meera: Yes, we'll include at least two model families and run side-by-side comparisons including reranking + retrieval + function-calling scenarios.
[06:52] [06:53] Liam: I'll follow up with the SOC2 and SAML docs and a pricing matrix. Meera will send the benchmark plan and propose pilot config (Dedicated pool size, model variants, synthetic load). Jules, you'll share sample prompts and QPS numbers.
[07:06] Jules: Great. Priya and I will prepare the infra checklist items and share the vector DB constraints.
[07:11] Priya: We'll also flag any data residency accounts that require on-prem.
[07:15] Meera: Quick note — if you need air-gapped for a subset, we can outline the on-prem package; there is additional lead time.
[07:22] Tomás: Good to know.
[07:24] [07:25] Liam: Alright, unless anyone has anything else we'll wrap. Thanks all. We'll follow up with the materials and calendar invite for the infra deep-dive.
[07:32] Jules: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:33] Meeting end.
